title: A linear threshold approximates a nearly maximal level-one function
statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every dimension $n$, every Boolean function $f$ on the sign cube, and every $0<\varepsilon\le1$ for which each level-one Fourier coefficient has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$ and the total Fourier weight at level one is at least $2/\pi-\varepsilon$, the relative Hamming distance from $f$ to the sign of its degree-one Fourier part is at most $C\sqrt{\varepsilon}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Every level-one Fourier coefficient has absolute value at most $\varepsilon$
The level-one Fourier weight is at least $2/\pi-\varepsilon$
A single constant $C>0$ works for all such choices
